rationale: Round 0 failed with a compiler internal error caused by extreme weights, so this table pulls every value toward the balanced midpoint (0.4-0.6) while keeping a mild security lean. SUB stays slightly favored since arithmetic-heavy kernels (Crystal_Cholesky, Crystal_div, Crystal_pow) benefit most from instruction substitution with low correctness risk. BCF and IBR get modest security and diversity boosts to add control-flow and branch indirection, tempered by RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights near 0.5 so the 5KB text footprint doesn't balloon. FLA and SPLIT sit at neutral values: flattening helps but the Cholesky loop nests are runtime-sensitive, and splitting a program with only 7 functions yields limited gain. ICALL carries a higher CorrectnessRisk weight to temper indirect-call dispatching on numeric code where indirect calls are riskiest, and IGV remains balanced as a low-cost global-variable complement. The narrow 0.4-0.6 band should avoid the compiler's degenerate selection behavior while still letting feature-match drive pass application.
